props.title: Robin Hood: Men in Tights
props.initialSlug: Mel Brooks spoofs Robin Hood with silly laughs

sections.content: Mel Brooks delivers another masterful parody with Robin Hood: Men in Tights, gleefully skewering both the Robin Hood legend and specifically Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves (1991). Brooks continues his tradition of genre satire established in Blazing Saddles (1974) and Spaceballs (1987), using Cary Elwes' pitch-perfect comedic timing to mock Kevin Costner's earnest portrayal. The film represents Brooks' last truly memorable comedy, featuring his signature mix of slapstick, wordplay, and anachronistic jokes that break the fourth wall.

sections.content: The film sits within Brooks' larger body of genre parodies, each targeting specific films while lampooning entire genres. Young Frankenstein (1974) lovingly mocked Universal monster movies, while Spaceballs (1987) took aim at Star Wars (1977) and space opera conventions. Men in Tights continues this tradition, with Dave Chappelle's Ahchoo character serving as a knowing wink to Morgan Freeman's Azeem, while Richard Lewis delivers a delightfully neurotic Prince John. SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Comedy Parody Films

While Airplane! (1980) and The Naked Gun (1988) established the rapid-fire parody style, Brooks' approach in Men in Tights maintains his preference for character-driven comedy and musical numbers. The film's influence can be seen in later parodies like Not Another Teen Movie (2001) and Scary Movie (1999), though few achieved Brooks' balance of pointed satire and genuine affection for the source material. The film's enduring popularity speaks to Brooks' understanding that successful parody requires both knowledge of and respect for the genre being satirized.
